title: Reciprocal gluing of the exceptional conic and pair of lines
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$. Let $E$ be the scheme obtained by gluing $L=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}k[r,s]/(rs-\epsilon)$, and $L'=\operatorname{Spec}k[h]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring] as follows. Glue $D(t)\subset L$ with $D(r)\subset V$ by $r=t^{-1},s=\epsilon t$, and $D(h)\subset L'$ with $D(s)\subset V$ by $s=h^{-1},r=\epsilon h$. If $\epsilon=1$ the outer opens overlap on $D(t)=D(h)$ with $h=t^{-1}$, and if $\epsilon=0$ they are disjoint. For $\epsilon=1$, $E$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_k$ [def-sc-p1-standard] and to the smooth plane conic
$$Q=\operatorname{Proj}k[X,P,Y]/(XY-P^2)$$
[def-nagata-affine-proj, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The isomorphism $E\to Q$ is given on the three charts by $[1:t:t^2]$, $[r:1:s]$, and $[h^2:h:1]$ respectively. The opens $D_+(X),D_+(Y)$ cover $Q$ and identify with the two outer affine lines; this includes characteristic two. For $\epsilon=0$, $E$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] with exactly two irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], each isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_k$, their scheme-theoretic intersection (the fibre product of the two closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]) is the single reduced point $(r,s)=(0,0)$, and the local equation there is $rs=0$. The $r$-axis completes with $L$ and the $s$-axis with $L'$. These identifications and intersection descriptions commute with extension of the ground field [def-pc-base-change].

proof.text: Put $A_\epsilon=k[r,s]/(rs-\epsilon)$. The principal-open localization theorem gives $(A_\epsilon)_r=k[r,r^{-1}]$, with $s=\epsilon r^{-1}$, and $(A_\epsilon)_s=k[s,s^{-1}]$, with $r=\epsilon s^{-1}$. Thus $r\mapsto t^{-1},s\mapsto\epsilon t$ and $s\mapsto h^{-1},r\mapsto\epsilon h$ are the required overlap ring isomorphisms. Their inverses send $t\mapsto r^{-1}$ and $h\mapsto s^{-1}$. If $\epsilon=1$, $D(r)=D(s)=V$ and the composite gives $h=s^{-1}=r=t^{-1}$; if $\epsilon=0$, $D(r)\cap D(s)=D(rs)=\varnothing$. These computations verify the triple-overlap condition. Apply scheme gluing to obtain the three specified open embeddings and their stated intersections.

Suppose $\epsilon=1$. Since all of $V$ is identified with $D(t)\subset L$, the two outer opens already cover $E$. Their overlap is $k[t,t^{-1}]$, with $h=t^{-1}$. The standard cover of $\mathbf P^1_k$ has exactly these rings and this transition. Use the identity on $k[t]$ and $k[h]$ to define maps in both directions on the two covers. Scheme-morphism gluing produces global maps, and its uniqueness clause shows both composites are the identity. Hence $E\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$.

Write $S=k[X,P,Y]/(XY-P^2)$, with all three variables of degree one. A homogeneous prime containing $X,Y$ contains $P^2$ and hence $P$, so cannot be a point of $\operatorname{Proj}S$. Thus $D_+(X),D_+(Y)$ cover $Q$. By the standard Proj affine-chart theorem their rings are
$$S_{(X),0}=k[a,b]/(b-a^2)\simeq k[a],\quad a=P/X,\ b=Y/X,$$
$$S_{(Y),0}=k[c,d]/(d-c^2)\simeq k[c],\quad c=P/Y,\ d=X/Y,$$
and $S_{(P),0}=k[r,s]/(rs-1)$, with $r=X/P,s=Y/P$. These presentations follow by dividing homogeneous degree-$m$ polynomials by the $m$th power of the chosen variable; the inverse substitutes $(1,a,a^2)$, $(c^2,c,1)$ or $(r,1,s)$, respectively. Every monomial fraction is a polynomial in these ratios, and substitution and inclusion are inverse. On $D_+(X)\cap D_+(Y)$, $a^2=Y/X$ is invertible, so $a$ is invertible and $c=a^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), Tag 00JP (algebra-lemma-topology-proj); explicit degree-zero quotient calculations

proof.text: The ring isomorphisms $a\mapsto t$ and $c\mapsto h$ identify the two outer charts with $D_+(X)$ and $D_+(Y)$. Their overlap relation is $h=t^{-1}$, the same as in step 2. Gluing these chart maps and their inverses, then using uniqueness on the covers, gives an isomorphism $E\to Q$. In homogeneous coordinates its restrictions are $[1:t:t^2]$ and $[h^2:h:1]$. On $V$, $r=t^{-1},s=t$; multiplying $[1:t:t^2]$ by the unit $t^{-1}$ gives $[r:1:s]$. Equivalently the middle-chart ring maps send $X/P\mapsto r,Y/P\mapsto s$, so this is equality of scheme maps, not only equality on $k$-points. The argument $P^2\in\mathfrak p\Rightarrow P\in\mathfrak p$ and all substitutions work in characteristic two.

Both outer charts of $Q$ are affine lines over $k$ with the structural map induced by the inclusion of constants. By the affine-space smoothness statement for $n=1$ they are smooth over $k$. Smoothness is local on the open cover of the source, so $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. This proves the claimed smoothness without using the derivative $2P$ or any assumption on the characteristic.

proof.text: Now suppose $\epsilon=0$. Glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[r]$ to $L$ along $r=t^{-1}$; glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$ to $L'$ along $s=h^{-1}$. By the standard projective-line cover and morphism gluing these schemes $C_r,C_s$ are each $\mathbf P^1_k$. On their axis charts define maps to $V$ by $A_0\to k[r]$, $s\mapsto0$, and $A_0\to k[s]$, $r\mapsto0$; on their outer charts use the given inclusions $L,L'\to E$. They agree on the overlaps by step 1 and hence glue to maps $C_r,C_s\to E$. For $C_r$, the inverse images of $L,V,L'$ are respectively $L,\operatorname{Spec}k[r],\varnothing$; for $C_s$ they are $\varnothing,\operatorname{Spec}k[s],L'$. This follows from the overlap formulas and $D(r)\cap V(s)=D(r)$, $D(s)\cap V(s)=\varnothing$, with the variables exchanged for $C_s$. Over these target charts the maps are identities, the displayed quotient maps, or the empty closed immersion. The affine characterization of closed immersions and locality on the target therefore make both maps closed immersions.

proof.text:
The ring $A_0$ has unique normal forms $c+rf(r)+sg(s)$, because the ideal $(rs)$ has exactly the monomials divisible by both $r$ and $s$. Hence the map
$$A_0\longrightarrow k[r]\times k[s],\quad F\longmapsto(F(r,0),F(0,s))$$
is injective: zero restrictions force each normal-form coefficient to vanish. Polynomial rings over a field are domains and therefore reduced; a nilpotent in their product, and thus in its subring $A_0$, is zero. The two outer chart rings are reduced for the same reason. The affine reducedness criterion followed by reducedness on an open cover proves $E$ reduced.

Every prime of $A_0$ contains $r$ or $s$, since $rs=0$. Thus the two closed images $C_r,C_s$ cover $V$, and their outer charts cover $L,L'$; hence they cover $E$. A polynomial domain $k[z]$ has the prime $(0)$ as a dense point of its spectrum: a closed set $V(I)$ containing $(0)$ has $I=0$. Thus each affine line is irreducible. In the reciprocal gluing defining each $C_r,C_s$, the two affine lines share the nonempty dense open $D(z)$. The generic points of their zero ideals are identified there, and their common image has closure containing both affine charts. It is therefore dense in the entire component, proving irreducibility. Neither closed image contains the other, since $L$ lies only in $C_r$ and $L'$ only in $C_s$. Any irreducible subset of their union lies in one of them: its two intersections with these closed sets give a finite closed cover. Consequently they are exactly the two maximal irreducible subsets of $E$.

source.place: Tag 01JE (example-projective-line); explicit prime-ideal and irreducible closed-cover argument

proof.text:
The two components cannot intersect outside $V$: on $L$ only $C_r$ occurs and on $L'$ only $C_s$ occurs. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is their fibre product over $E$, so on $V$ the affine fibre-product theorem identifies its ring with
$$ (A_0/(s))\otimes_{A_0}(A_0/(r))=A_0/(r,s)=k.$$
For the displayed tensor equality, maps from either ring to a commutative ring are exactly compatible maps from both quotients, equivalently a map from $A_0$ killing $r$ and $s$. This also verifies that the intersection is the reduced single point, not a thickening. The ambient affine neighbourhood $V$ is precisely $\operatorname{Spec}k[r,s]/(rs)$; thus its local ring at the intersection is $(k[r,s]/(rs))_{(r,s)}$, giving the asserted local equation $rs=0$.

source.place: Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); explicit quotient tensor universal property

proof.text: Let $k\to K$ be any field extension. Base change of an open immersion is an open immersion, with image the inverse image of its original open: this image assertion follows from the fibre-product universal property for maps factoring through an open subscheme. The pulled-back charts therefore cover $E_K$. Their affine fibre-product rings are $K[t],K[r,s]/(rs-\epsilon),K[h]$: the isomorphisms send $a\otimes F$ to $aF$ with the coefficients of $F$ mapped to $K$, and their inverses send each coordinate to $1\otimes$ that coordinate. The overlap substitutions are unchanged on each generator. On the conic charts the same formula gives $K[a,b]/(b-a^2)$, $K[c,d]/(d-c^2)$ and $K[r,s]/(rs-1)$; hence the conic over $K$ is identified with $Q_K$ by gluing these isomorphisms and their inverses. All parametrizations from step 4, axis quotient maps from step 6, and the quotient $A_0/(r,s)=k$ from step 9 extend by exactly these coefficient maps. Equality on coordinate generators and uniqueness of glued morphisms prove compatibility of all identifications and of the intersection with ground-field extension. Repeating step 8 over $K$ shows the two components stay precisely two components.
